title: MAGA Is In Turmoil Over Tucker Carlson’s Possible 2028 Presidential Bid
gist: A coalition of prominent MAGA-aligned figures — Marjorie Taylor Greene, Thomas Massie, and Joe Kent — is publicly pushing Tucker Carlson to run a third-party 'America First' presidential bid in 2028 over grievances that Trump betrayed promises to end foreign wars and release the Epstein files, triggering visible backlash from other pro-Trump influencers and exposing a real fracture within the MAGA coalition ahead of the November midterms.

themes.theme: A new anti-Trump MAGA faction takes shape

insights.claim: Former US representative Marjorie Taylor Greene shared a photo taken at Tucker Carlson's Maine cabin showing herself, Carlson, former representative Thomas Massie, and former National Counterterrorism Center head Joe Kent, announcing a new coalition aimed at running a third-party candidate in the 2028 presidential election, with Carlson as their top choice.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: A visible, named coalition of sitting-adjacent MAGA figures organizing a third-party 2028 challenge is a concrete early data point for anyone tracking fracture risk within the Republican coalition ahead of the 2026 midterms and the 2028 cycle.
insights.quote: We said no more foreign wars and we meant it and supported Donald Trump because he made that promise. But he's betrayed us all. Our commitment is America First for all Americans, right, left, and center. The movement has begun.
insights.locator: Greene wrote in a caption accompanying the photo

insights.claim: The group's stated grievances are that Trump failed to uphold campaign promises to end foreign wars and to release the Epstein files, and Joe Kent said the group is also exploring how to get a third-party candidate on the ballot in all 50 states, citing Robert F. Kennedy's struggles getting on ballots ahead of the 2024 election as the operational challenge they need to solve.
insights.speaker: Joe Kent (via David Gilbert)
insights.so_what: Naming ballot access as the specific operational obstacle (with RFK's 2024 struggles as the reference case) indicates this is a serious logistical planning effort, not just a symbolic gesture — worth watching for follow-through on state-by-state filings.
insights.quote: I'd say all of us at one point in time told Tucker he needs to run, and Tucker's been pretty public that he's not going to run.
insights.locator: Kent appeared on The Young Turks show

insights.claim: Despite the coalition's public campaign, Carlson has repeatedly and publicly stated, including as recently as late June, that he does not plan to run for office, and did not respond to WIRED's request for comment.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Carlson's own repeated denials mean the movement currently has no confirmed candidate at its center, making the coalition's near-term viability uncertain regardless of its organizing momentum.
insights.locator: In late June, Carlson reiterated that he did not plan to run

themes.theme: Visible backlash exposes the coalition's fragility

insights.claim: Prominent pro-Trump MAGA influencers publicly attacked the new coalition, including Laura Loomer calling Carlson 'a lunatic' who 'wants to hijack the GOP,' and influencer Phillip Buchanan ('Catturd') writing that the group has 'zero pull anymore' and calling them a 'table full of laughingstocks.'
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Sharp, public pushback from other high-profile pro-Trump influencers signals the new coalition faces significant intra-movement resistance and lacks unified MAGA-world backing, reducing the near-term likelihood of a broadly supported third-party bid.
insights.quote: He's a lunatic! Tucker wants to hijack the GOP in 2026 and 2028.
insights.locator: Laura Loomer, a staunch Trump supporter, wrote on X

insights.claim: White-nationalist creator Nick Fuentes, who sparked controversy within MAGA after Carlson interviewed him, dismissed the new group's efforts, predicting the movement will lack a strong message on religion, race, or immigration without him, and claimed its members will ultimately end up supporting JD Vance in 2028.
insights.speaker: Nick Fuentes (via David Gilbert)
insights.so_what: Fuentes' prediction that the group ultimately defaults to backing Vance in 2028 offers a specific, named alternative outcome to watch for if the third-party effort loses steam.
insights.quote: They are going to try to create this America First movement without me, but it has to exclude me because it will also be without any kind of strong message on religion, race, or maybe even immigration.

insights.claim: The White House dismissed the coalition, with spokesperson Davis Ingle stating that Trump 'remains the unequivocal leader of the Republican Party' and describing the photo as 'an embarrassing collection of mostly whiny turncoats who dramatically overestimate their influence and relevance.'
insights.speaker: Davis Ingle (via David Gilbert)
insights.so_what: The White House's dismissive, combative response rather than conciliatory outreach suggests the administration currently views the breakaway faction as a minor irritant rather than a serious electoral threat requiring engagement.
insights.quote: this photo represents an embarrassing collection of mostly whiny turncoats who dramatically overestimate their influence and relevance.
insights.locator: White House spokesperson Davis Ingle tells WIRED
